scenario_stem:
A regional department store chain operates 5 retail stores as a Public Limited Company, employing 200 shop floor assistants and 25 middle managers across 5 hierarchical management levels. Operating for 15 years, the company generates $12m in annual sales revenue, but fixed wage overheads have surged to $4.2m.

Due to aggressive price competition from online e-commerce retailers, store profits have fallen by 20%. The tall organizational hierarchy results in a long chain of command and narrow spans of control (4 subordinates per manager), causing customer feedback on product pricing to take weeks to reach executive directors. Store managers report being micro-managed and unable to launch local sales promotions without head-office authorization. To lower fixed costs and speed up market response, the board is evaluating delayering (removing 2 middle management levels to flatten the structure) versus downsizing shop floor assistants.

questions.question_text: Define 'delayering'.
questions.model_answer: Removing one or more management levels from an organizational hierarchy to create a flatter structure [2].

questions.model_answer: Problem 1: Slow communication speed [k], as customer feedback on pricing takes weeks to pass through 5 management levels [app]. Problem 2: Message distortion [k], as instructions regarding local sales promotions are altered as they pass down to 200 shop floor staff [app].

Benefit 2: Wider spans of control and greater delegation [k], allowing store managers to approve local promotions quickly [app], improving responsiveness to e-commerce competitors [an].
